messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for runtime-serving-prod — trigger: `inference_p95_latency > 500ms` (window 2m). PD INC: #PDR-8123 :rotating_light:
pd-notify: PagerDuty notification sent to: @mike.s (primary), @julia (secondary). Escalation policy: severe-latency-rotation.
mike.s: acked. Taking first touch — oncall ramping up. I'll grab logs + top pods.
julia: thx. I'm pulling the dashboard: p95 spiked to ~620ms across two clusters (us-west-2a/b). Error rate up ~0.7% (503 gateway) — might be KV cache thrash or a transient burst.
liz_sre: can you check `cache_hit_ratio` and `inflight_batches` on the serving nodes? last time a similar blip was KV warmup causing backpressure.
mike.s: running quick checks:
```
kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=serve -o wide
kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/serve-runtime --tail=200 | grep -E "WARN|ERROR|KVCache" | tail -n 60
```
Found some repeated `KVCache miss` messages and an uptick in `batch_wait_time` on node serve-12.
ron_platform: I see autoscaler bumped replicas earlier then dropped — looks like a short burst of requests caused a scale spike that completed then some pods reported higher tail latencies. Might be cold KV shards after a deploy-ish pattern.
maya_support: any customer-facing errors? Support stats show 4 customers with a handful of 5xxs in the last 3m, nothing widespread but one enterprise account saw ~10 failed requests. I'm prepping a short note in case they reach out.
julia: good catch. Let's avoid noisy escalations: if PD is configured to auto-suppress flapping we should let it settle for a couple minutes unless p95 stays > 500 for 5m. I'm going to temporarily increase the alerting window to 5m on the ops dashboard (manual view) to confirm trend.
liz_sre: given pattern, two mitigation options: (1) force warm KV cache on the affected nodes, (2) route new traffic to fallback model variant with lower memory working set. Option 1 is lower risk.
mike.s: running cache warm command on the affected pod group: `curl -X POST http://serve-12.runtime.internal/_warm_kv?shard=12` — firing on 3 pods.
ron_platform: watching metrics, `cache_hit_ratio` climbing back to baseline, `batch_wait_time` dropping.
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: INC #PDR-8123 acknowledged by mike.s at 2468001236. Auto-escalation timer paused.
maya_support: communicated a brief note to the single affected customer: "We're investigating transient inference errors, potential performance impact has been mitigated; we'll follow up if anything changes."
mike.s: p95 back to ~330ms across zones, 503 errors dropped to baseline. Looks like quick warm fixed it.
julia: nice. Since this was brief and we saw spike+recover within ~1.5m, PD may auto-resolve if it believes noise. We should still add a small action item: add a lightweight KV warm during pod start to avoid cold-shard bursts.
liz_sre: +1. Recommend adding a post-start hook with `GET /_warm_kv?limit=100` and a telemetry check. I'll add a GH draft.
ron_platform: I'll also parameterize the autoscaler cooldown to avoid quick downscale after transient burst (currently 60s downscale window). Maybe bump to 3m.
incident-bot: Auto-resolve: PagerDuty incident #PDR-8123 has been marked resolved (reason: alert returned to below threshold).
mike.s: resolving here as well. Leaving a short handoff note for next oncall: this was a transient KV-cold issue causing short p95 spikes and a handful of 503s for one customer. Mitigation: warmed KV shards; proposed long-term: startup warm + longer scaler cooldown.
julia: noted. I'll add the incident to the daily wakeup for a quick triage and decide owners for the GH PRs.
maya_support: will follow up with the customer if they open a ticket; we already sent a heads up.
liz_sre: created GH draft: "kv-warm-startup-hook" and assigned to ron_platform + liz_sre.
mike.s: handing off to night oncall — @julia you're up for the overnight watch. If this flaps again, escalate to infra-sre policy.
julia: on it. good pickup everyone. :thumbsup:
